name: Schnapsen
description: Schnapsen is a two-player Austrian marriage-group point-trick game played with a 20-card pack. Players try to be first to 66 points by taking valuable tricks and declaring marriages. The game has an open-talon phase followed by stricter play after the talon is exhausted or closed.

content.text: Schnapsen is a two-player Austrian marriage-group point-trick game played with a 20-card pack. Players try to be first to 66 points by taking valuable tricks and declaring marriages. The game has an open-talon phase followed by stricter play after the talon is exhausted or closed.

Schnapsen is an Austrian two-player form of the wider Sechsundsechzig or Sixty-Six family. It is described as a tightened version of the German game Sechsundsechzig and is closely related to games such as Bauernschnapsen, Talon-Schnapsen, Tute, Tyziacha, and Snapszli.
Exactly two players sit opposite each other.
Use 20 cards: Ace, Ten, King, Queen or Ober, and Jack or Unter in each suit. Card points are A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q/O=3, J/U=2.
A 20-card Schnapsen pack and a score sheet or counters for game points.
Deal five cards to each player. Turn one card face up to establish trump and place the remaining stock crosswise on it as the talon.

items.text: Three-Handed Schnapsen: A three-player adaptation of the two-player game in which the deal and table structure are changed for an extra player.
Talon-Schnapsen: A related talon form in the Schnapsen family.
